parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a national document/entry regime (binary sex markers, no X processing, cable ordering refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with a considered lifetime fraud bar) onto a state ranked among the worst for anti-trans legislation. Universal exposures are documented: facility exclusion in state-run buildings, a birth-certificate marker ban, no state discrimination statute, and a state hate-crime law omitting gender identity. Tier-1 features exist: a documented 2025 arrest with 24 hours' hold in a men's ward, federal conversion-therapy-style inmate policy, and immigration-custody abuse reports. Mitigating: functioning courts, active injunctions, national employment and hate-crime protections, 78% public support for non-discrimination, and no dated trans violence incident recorded. Net: Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 executive order and cable: no X or identity-matched markers for new documents; officer instructed to refuse where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and to consider a permanent fraud-based lifetime ineligibility. Trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, some stranded abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; the policy is under active litigation by a civil-liberties union; a legal-aid organisation runs a standing FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Visa-stage refusal by a post strands a traveller before arrival; state ID/birth-certificate closure affects only residents, so the visitor's home passport governs — but presentation mismatch still triggers the cable's refusal logic.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented 19 March 2025 arrest of a transgender woman in a capitol women's restroom, charged with trespass (up to 60 days), held 24 hours in the men's ward. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style inmate policies from 2026; trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The statute requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart when asked, not automatic arrest; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts are functioning and several orders are enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A state misdemeanor arrest routes a visitor into birth-sex custody placement, where documented federal custody practices apply to held trans people.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law (April 2023, effective 1 July) explicitly permits restricting trans people's bathroom use in many state-run facilities; the national order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. Four states criminalise use in certain circumstances; this state's trespass route is documented once.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Most mapped bans reach government-owned settings only; statutory exemptions cover assistance, emergencies and maintenance; 29 state/provinces and the capital district have no such ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering a capitol, state park, DMV or state university carries both the federal funding rule and the state permission rule simultaneously.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is illegal in the state (April 2023, veto-proof). National funding freezes, a proposed insurance rule, an executive order calling such care 'mutilation', and DOJ subpoenas of under-19 patient records narrow access and raise disclosure risk.
care_services.protection: No documented refusal of emergency care to adult visitors; a 2021 state regulation bans conversion therapy by state counsellors; national employment protection survives.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor who needs routine or emergency care faces a state where providers may be criminalised, pushing care-seeking toward investigation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; a Dec 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist framing; an executive order directs law enforcement to investigate schools and prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo states the phrase is never a criterion; the strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; multiple orders are blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises both outing probability during any police encounter and the severity of how an outed traveller is treated.

minors_guardians.exposure: State law requires disclosure of transgender students to parents in state-run schools; state bans trans minors' care; the national order threatens criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition using names or pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: National employment and hate-crime protections apply; no documented prosecution of a travelling parent; conversion therapy is banned for state counsellors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's trans minor can be outed through any school, clinic or document interaction, converting a care need into a provider-investigation exposure for the parent.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law does not cover gender identity; no state-level anti-discrimination statute; a 2021 party platform accused transgender people of preying on women; a religious-refusal service bill passed with disposition unrecorded.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; a 2022 poll found 78% support for an LGBT non-discrimination law; advocacy groups publicly condemned the arrest; no dated trans violence incident appears in the sources.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of incident data in an otherwise well-documented country is weakly positive, not proof of safety; national employment protection supplies a floor absent state law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Most national measures are in unresolved litigation, so exposure shifts with the moment of travel; the state's hate-crime law and discrimination gap persist; the birth-certificate statute/regulation relationship and the religious-refusal bill's fate are unrecorded.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts, multiple injunctions, an active civil-liberties suit over passports, a legal-aid FAQ, and national equality rulings show remedies operating at least partly.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy availability varies by state and date, so a traveller cannot predict outcomes of a refusal, arrest or service denial in real time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra imposes universal entry exclusion with no remedy. Here the entry-cable refusal is discretionary, contested in court, and the lifetime bar is a considered never-automatic finding — comparable exposure. But this dossier adds documented arrest with birth-sex custody (worse than exclusion) alongside functioning courts, national protections and 78% public support (better). Net slightly above.

Closest match: routine exposure at checkpoints and services, detention and humiliation documented, prosecutions uncommon, remedies narrow, enforcement inconsistent and guidance shifting without notice. This dossier is marginally lower on one axis — a documented arrest with 24-hour men's-ward placement — and marginally higher on public-opinion and litigation evidence.

Kestrel Isles offers only administrative refusal with an appeal desk and consular notice. This jurisdiction sits below it: entry refusal can escalate to a permanent fraud-based ineligibility, and a documented state facility arrest with birth-sex custody is a criminal pathway that 0.55-B lacks.

Meridia trains border officers, guarantees written reasons and compensation, and detention ends in release. Well above this dossier: here document mismatch triggers a refusal instruction, facilities are lawfully restricted, no state discrimination or hate-crime protection exists, and custody placement by birth sex is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Two sovereign layers compound. The national regime makes document and entry exposure universal for trans travellers: markers fixed at birth, no X processing, an instruction to refuse on any sex discrepancy, and a considered lifetime fraud bar — with real reports of blocked passports. The state adds facility exclusion permission, a closed birth-certificate regime, no state discrimination statute, and a hate-crime law omitting gender identity; one arrest with 24-hour men's-ward custody proves the pathway is live, and federal custody practices (conversion-therapy-style inmate policies, immigration-abuse reports) apply once detained. Against this, courts function, several orders are enjoined, national employment and hate-crime protections stand, and 78% back non-discrimination. Severity stops short of long imprisonment: the worst documented custody is hours, the state offense caps at 60 days, and no execution or trans killing is recorded — so Elevated, not High, Risk.
